items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: Socarras, a flute player, a Cuban flute player that toured a lot, Alberto Socarras, he is one of the guys that taught in New York

ctx.x: Oh sort of like a jazz tune, you’ve got the head at the beginning and at the end.

Right. So you go back, but in the middle they did a dance part for the people, and that’s where the Latin part came in. But you would start off at a sweet, and then a certain break [scats] and that’s when everybody starts going crazy and dancing but, and after that you would finish [scats] you know, to end it off. So if you’re going to study charanga, flute players, sax and flute players listen to a lot of — flute players will listen to a charanga music because that’s a whole style in itself. Socarras, a flute…

is like one of the guys from Cuba, old school guys that had that style, that grew up in that style. Jose Fajardo, flute. They played the black, Cuban flute, the wooden flute, five holes, open holed, open holed.
